analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES – Amazon misses buyside; VMED looks to wholesale; CAP raises; UMG beats; INTEL guides below; ETL misses
key_insights: Amazon fell about 11% after hours. AWS grew 39.3% to $46.0bn, ahead of sellside at 37.7% but below buyside expectations of around 43%. AWS operating margin of 38.7% missed the roughly 40% investors wanted.

Amazon group operating income was $28.1bn vs consensus $26.2bn, but advertising missed ($19.6B vs Street $20.9B). Q4 guidance top ends of $247bn revenue and $33.5bn operating income were below buyside expectations, with both midpoints below Street.
Amazon cash capex of $75.9bn pushed trailing-12-month free cash flow to -$42.4bn, adding to the funding debate. Jassy projected AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

Hyperscaler read-through from the desk: AI demand is not the constraint, capacity and the cost of delivering it are. AWS reported $46.0bn (+39%), Azure $33.2bn, Google Cloud $30.7bn (+103%). Two hyperscalers flagged third-party AI chip/capacity delays pushing some capacity into 1H27, and Q3 capex came in light while full-year guides stayed elevated.

Intel fell about 17% after hours. Q3 DCAI revenue was $7.3bn, +78% y/y, but 4Q guidance was well below the Street: revenue $15.5bn midpoint vs GS $18.0bn and Street $17.0bn, non-GAAP gross margin 38% vs Street 42.5%, non-GAAP EPS $0.25 vs Street $0.43. Intel expects a PC slowdown through at least H1 2027 on memory price/availability and OEM inventory discipline.

Capgemini beat and raised. Q3 organic growth was 5.2% vs sellside 3.9%. FY organic growth guide raised to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4% (Street 4.1%). Operating margin (13.6-13.8%) and organic FCF (€1.8-1.9B) guides unchanged. Book-to-bill of 89% vs a seasonal norm of 95-96% is the bear point.

UMG was far better than feared. Streaming subscription growth ex downtown was 9.5% vs Street around 8.5% and bears at 6-7%. Margin was 21.5%, 90bps ahead of Street. GIR nudged FY2026+ revenue and adjusted EBITDA up by about 0-1%. AI-generated track uploads rose from 10,000 a day in Q1 2025 to almost 100,000 a day.

Sandisk was unchanged after beating on revenue, gross margin and EPS. It announced an 8-for-1 split and repurchased about $5bn of shares. Q4 guidance of $12.4bn revenue and EPS $55-57 beat Street $12.08bn and $52.94. The stock is down about 20% over 30 days.

Eutelsat (ETL) missed revenue by 4%, driven by an 8% miss in Video. Connectivity and Government were in line. Fixed connectivity missed as customers moved from GEO to LEO, where Eutelsat is subscale vs Starlink. FY targets reiterated.
Twilio fell about 15%. Q3 organic revenue grew 16% y/y (17% prior quarter) and the Q4 organic growth outlook disappointed. The desk reads it negatively for Sinch.

BT rose 5% on an FT report that Virgin Media O2 is finalizing a wholesale deal to use Openreach for expansion outside its footprint while freezing its own cable-to-fibre upgrades. VMO2 faces credit stress on its £22bn debt, and a regulatory block of the £2bn Nexfibre deal removed a planned £1.1bn cash injection.

STMicro call was solid and the desk expects the Street to raise estimates by mid-single digits. Management said it is comfortable meeting Q1 revenue consensus within the 86-day quarter, sees no pull-forward in Q3 personal electronics, is raising prices on selected products, and expects satellite revenue next year to match or exceed this year's record.
Proximus was mixed. Revenue and EBITDA were in line, with domestic EBITDA missing (-1.8% vs expectations), but lower capex gave an OFCF beat. Strong Global performance led to upgraded FY guidance.

Crypto disruption: Binance suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover losses after an attack affecting an estimated $6.3bn of funds. Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange after a third-party software provider was compromised.
Elisa: GIR sees a slower Finnish service-revenue recovery, with even the low end of FY26 0-2% telecom growth guidance at risk. Rating is Neutral, lowered from Buy in September.

US Telcos: FCC proposal 26-71 would expand eligible Supplemental Coverage from Space spectrum from five to 13 bands, adding 482MHz, and allow local-area service, easing direct-to-phone satellite connectivity for Starlink and AST SpaceMobile.

Q4 guide tops: revenue $247bn, operating income $33.5bn.

Intel Q3 (reported): revenue and gross margin in line to beat, gross margin 44.1%, DCAI revenue $7.3bn +78% y/y. Q4 guidance: revenue $15.5bn midpoint (GS $18.0bn, Street $17.0bn), non-GAAP gross margin 38% (GS 43.6%, Street 42.5%), non-GAAP EPS $0.25 (GS $0.46, Street $0.43).

Capgemini Q3 (reported): organic growth 5.2% vs sellside 3.9%. FY guide raised to 4-4.5% organic growth (prior 3.5-4%, Street 4.1%). Operating margin 13.6-13.8% and organic FCF €1.8-1.9B unchanged. Book-to-bill 89%.
UMG Q3 (reported): streaming subscription growth ex downtown 9.5% (Street about 8.5%), margin 21.5%, 90bps above Street.
Sandisk (reported): beat on revenue, gross margin and EPS. Q4 guidance: revenue $12.4bn (Street est $12.08bn), EPS $55-57 (Street est $52.94).
Eutelsat (reported): revenue missed by 4%, Video missed by 8%, Connectivity and Government in line. FY targets reiterated.
Proximus (reported): revenue in line, EBITDA in line, domestic EBITDA -1.8% vs expectations, OFCF beat on lower capex, FY guidance upgraded on Global.
Twilio Q3 (reported): organic revenue +16% y/y vs 17% last quarter; Q4 organic growth outlook weak.
STMicro (reported): management comfortable with Q1 revenue consensus within the 86-day quarter; Q3 personal electronics strength reflected demand.
Elisa: GIR sees FY26 consensus telecom growth of 0.3% and FY27 of 1.7% (estimates) at modest downside risk; company guidance is 0-2% for FY26.

Options market pricing of the next-session S&P move.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex and FCF pressure: Amazon trailing-12-month FCF of -$42.4bn adds to the funding debate.
Chip, power and data-centre constraints, with third-party AI chip delays pushing some capacity into 1H27.
PC slowdown through at least H1 2027 on memory pricing/availability and OEM inventory discipline (Intel).
Credit stress on VMO2's £22bn debt and a possible liability management exercise.
GEO to LEO migration eroding Eutelsat's connectivity business.
vol_and_positioning: Vol crush for most of the session: QQQ front-month fixed strike vols were offered down a vol at the lows and SPY vols fell more than 80 bps of vol. VIX futures moved nominally lower.
Skew was bid on the move lower, particularly in SPX gamma tenors. A customer bought 15k SPX 31Mar 5500 puts as a crash hedge.
Clients hedged single-name tech exposure and sparsely added convexity in higher-conviction positions.

AI complex (GSTMTAIP -1.5%) was used as a source of funds for everything else (SPXXAI +1.5%). Floor activity was 5 on a 1-10 scale, asset managers slight net sellers, hedge fund flows about flat, SPX volumes +35% vs 20-day average.
geopolitical: Regulatory opposition signalled a block of the £2bn Nexfibre transaction in the UK.
VMO2 CEO called for a full investigation into BT's TalkTalk acquisition and criticised the CMA's two-week review deadline.
